# Lock Opportunity Amount after Closed Won

<!-- Generated by scripts/build_plan.py render — never hand-edit. -->

Add a single ValidationRule on Opportunity that blocks any save reducing Amount once StageName is Closed Won, using PRIORVALUE(Amount) guarded against insert, with a named bypass for exempt users/integrations and an error message that states the problem and the fix; scoped to one metadata artefact with no new object, field, or automation.

## Defaults applied

- `Q4` — What should the validation error say, in 255 characters or fewer, naming both the problem and the fix?: Use the proposed default message as written. (source: skill-guidance)

## Answers given

- `Q1` — Does the Sales team enter Amount directly on the Opportunity, or is Amount rolling up from Opportunity Products / Line Items?: Amount is typed directly on the Opportunity by the rep. We do not use Opportunity Products / line items, so nothing rolls up into Amount.
- `Q2` — Does any Workflow Rule field update, Process Builder, or other automation write to Opportunity Amount after the record saves?: No. There are no Workflow Rule field updates or Process Builder processes on Opportunity, and the one record-triggered Flow we have only writes NextStep. Nothing writes Amount after save.
- `Q3` — Which users, profiles, or integrations must still be able to save a Closed Won Opportunity that would otherwise violate this rule (e.g. data loads, an ERP/CPQ sync, a manager issuing a credit memo, admins correcting an error) — and who is the accountable owner when the rule blocks a save that should have gone through?: Only the Sales Ops team (two people) may correct a Closed Won Amount, and only via a documented bypass: grant them a custom permission checked by the rule (a permission set assigned to them), not a profile exemption. No integration user writes Amount.
- `Q5` — Does Opportunity data today already violate this rule — are there Closed Won Opportunities whose Amount has already been edited downward, or a legitimate recurring reason Amount decreases after close (refunds, credit memos, contract true-ups)?: Yes, a handful of Closed Won Opportunities have had Amount lowered historically. Leave them as they are; no data clean-up is in scope. The rule only needs to stop it from now on.
- `Q6` — Roughly how many Opportunities move to Closed Won per day, and what is the largest single batch write to Opportunity anyone runs (data load, mass reassignment, a nightly sync)?: About 30 Opportunities move to Closed Won per day. The largest batch write is a quarterly Data Loader update of roughly 5,000 Opportunities that changes StageName and CloseDate but never Amount.
- `Q7` — Does Amount on a Closed Won Opportunity ever get written from outside Salesforce — an ERP, a CPQ tool, a billing system, or any inbound integration?: No. No ERP, CPQ or billing system writes Opportunity Amount; the only writers are Sales Cloud users in the UI and the quarterly Data Loader run in Q6, which does not touch Amount.

## Open questions

- `Q8` — Is Amount visible on every Opportunity page layout and for every record type this rule applies to? (proposed default: Amount is on the standard Opportunity layout(s) in scope; attach the error to the Amount field.)
- `Q9` — Does the rule's formula need to reference a compound field (Address, a person's Name) or a dependent picklist anywhere? (proposed default: No — the rule references only Amount (Currency) and StageName (Picklist), neither of which is a compound field.)
- `Q10` — Is there a workaround the team uses today to catch an Amount decrease after Closed Won (a report someone checks, a manual review), or is this a gap with no current safeguard? (proposed default: No current safeguard; the requirement itself states Amount 'can't go down' today, implying no control currently prevents it.)
- `Q11` — Does this change require any new record-access or field-level-security restriction, or does the existing Opportunity sharing/FLS model apply unchanged? (proposed default: No new record-access or FLS change requested; the existing Opportunity sharing and field-level-security model applies unchanged.)
- `Q12` — Who exactly edits Opportunity Amount — an internal employee, or does a customer, partner, or contractor with portal access ever touch it? (proposed default: Internal Sales Cloud users (employees) only, consistent with the requester (Sales Ops) and no portal/partner access implied by the requirement.)
- `Q13` — Does this requirement need a new report or dashboard number alongside the rule (e.g. a count of blocked saves), or is the rule a save-time control only? (proposed default: No new report requested; this is a save-time control only, not a reporting change.)

## Manual acceptance

- Given a Closed Won Opportunity, when a user without the Bypass_Opp_Amount_Lock permission lowers Amount and saves, then the save is blocked and the error reads 'Amount cannot be decreased once this Opportunity is Closed Won. Amount is locked after close to protect the recorded deal value. Contact your manager to reopen the Opportunity before changing Amount.'; when a Sales Ops user holding the Opp_Amount_Lock_Bypass permission set makes the identical edit, then the save succeeds.
